'''Mintil''' (alternatively '''Batek Tanum''', '''Tanɨm''', or '''Mayah''') is an [[Aslian language]] of [[Malaysia]]. It is considered to be a variety of the [[Batek language]]. 

==Background==
{{expand section|date=February 2021}}
In the late 1960s, Geoffrey Benjamin had come across speakers of Mintil among patients of an Orang Asli hospital at Ulu Gombak, just outside [[Kuala Lumpur]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Benjamin |first=Geoffrey |url=http://www.elpublishing.org/PID/131 |title=Language Documentation and Description, Volume 11 |date=2012 |publisher=Endangered Languages Project, School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS) |editor-last=Austin |editor-first=Peter K. |location=London |pages=136–230 |chapter=The Aslian languages of Malaysia and Thailand: An Assessment |editor-last2=McGill |editor-first2=Stuart}}</ref>

==Names and villages==
The people are commonly referred to as [[Batek people|Batek]]. There are 400 speakers of Mintil in [[Lipis District]], [[Pahang]] who call themselves {{lang|mzt|Batɛik}} ‘in-group people’, {{lang|mzt|Batɛik Tɔm Tanɨm}} ‘people of the [[Tanum River]]’, and {{lang|mzt|Batɛik Mayah}} {{IPA|[ba'tɛik may'ãh]|lang=mzt}}. Their villages are:<ref name="Lim">{{Cite journal |last=Lim |first=Teckwyn |date=2020 |title=Ethnolinguistic Notes on the Language Endangerment Status of Mintil, an Aslian Language |journal=Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society |language=en |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=i–xiv |hdl-access=free |hdl=10524/52461}}</ref>

*Kampung Sungai Garam (Tɔm Mayɛm) (4° 27’ 12” N, 102° 3’ 20” E; 2.5 km south of Kampung Dada Kering)
*Kampung Bencah Kelubi (Batuˀ Jalaŋ) (4° 38’ 23” N, 101° 58’ 45” E; 4 km east of Kampung Telok Gunong)
*Kampung Paya Keladi (Tɔm Hɨyaŋ) (4° 24’ 18” N, 101° 55’ 27” E; 10 km north of Kampung Chegar Perah)
*Kampung Tɔm Kəlkɔəˀ (4° 34’ 39” N, 101° 59’ 43” E; 2 km north of Kampung Kubang Rusa)
